clue.text: The first person in a position to order fish

indicators.note: in tells us the pronoun is set inside the word meaning a position

parts.note: a place is a position or spot
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone at the head of a queue is well placed to order a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside PLACE; 'to order' is a link here, though it reads like an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice is a European flatfish sold for eating.

clue.text: They offer support to the workers down under

definitions.text: They offer support to the workers down under

parts.words: They offer support to the workers down under
parts.note: down under suggests Australia, but the workers are miners down a shaft, and these timbers hold the roof up above them

explanation.surface: Supporters of Australian labour are being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Props are timber posts that hold up the roof of a coal mine's tunnels above the men working there.

clue.text: It's hard for a worker to hold the barricade

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
a worker is an ant, the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer finds it tough to man the barricades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard' is a noun definition: this word once named a legendary unbreakable stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was a name for an impossibly hard mineral, later the diamond, so it is something hard.

clue.text: Spanish or' Italians — possibly under a hundred

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the rearranged letters below the hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of Italians may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A remark about whether Spaniards or Italians number fewer than a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram of the second word to yield ASTILIAN; 'under' works because this is a down entry, so it sits below the Roman hundred. The page prints a stray mark after 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Castilian is the standard form of the Spanish language, from the region of Castile.

clue.text: Clean fellow, but a bit of a swine

parts.note: to bath someone is to clean them
a chap is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A man who washes well but behaves rather piggishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a swine' seems to call the fellow nasty; literally it is a part of a pig, a bath chap being cured pig's cheek, a British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath chap is the lower cheek of a pig, cured and cooked, so literally a piece of the animal.

clue.text: What one may tell oneself is the aim of a car advertisement

definitions.meaning: a self-induced idea or belief planted in one's own mind

definitions.text: the aim of a car advertisement
definitions.meaning: read as two words, an advert for a motor aims to put a hint about the vehicle in buyers' heads

explanation.surface: Musing on self-talk and the purpose of motor adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names influencing one's own mind by repeated ideas; split, it is a motor plus a hint, which is what a motoring advert offers.

clue.text: Harry a university man, though game

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
an MA is a Master of Arts, a university graduate

explanation.surface: Harry is a graduate but also a sporting type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like an adjective meaning willing, but it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which pieces jump across a square board, a forerunner of Chinese chequers.

clue.text: Listen to X and cheer

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Hearing a kiss, signed X, lifts someone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to encourage them, to raise their spirits.

clue.text: A club that's quiet, say

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A golf club described as a quiet one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' tag; here it is the verb meaning speak.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the golf club used for rolling the ball along the green into the hole.

clue.text: Not thinking to broadcast and breathe fire

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the three words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A thoughtless person would announce they breathe fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flighty and silly is not using their head, scatterbrained.

clue.text: Being only temporary, this may be modified instanter

indicators.note: may be modified suggests the letters of instanter can be reworked into another word

explanation.surface: A remark that a legal word for immediately is itself short-lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instanter' is an old legal word meaning at once, apt to a clue about brevity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing or fleeting lasts only a short time.

clue.text: Took off the French fitting

parts.note: le is French for the
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone removed a fixture of French make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' suggests removed; it means jumped.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off from the ground is to spring or jump.

clue.text: No dreamer where a schedule's concerned!

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a schedule is a list

explanation.surface: Practical people are hard-headed about timetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' joins; 'concerned' gives RE, which goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic person faces facts rather than living in fantasy.

clue.text: Decide to imbibe a large port

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in a drink, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it

explanation.surface: Making up one's mind to drink a big glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major harbour city in Washington State, USA.

clue.text: The artist's little boys pose half-time

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it

indicators.note: half asks for the first two of the four letters of time

explanation.surface: Painted cherubs strike a pose during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' reads as a football break; it is an instruction to halve TIME, giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are small naked cherubic boys found in Renaissance paintings.

clue.text: Quite charming — promising too

definitions.meaning: pledging, binding oneself by a promise

explanation.surface: Someone delightful who also shows potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promising' looks like 'full of promise'; it means pledging.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means delightful, and also pledging, as when a couple become betrothed.

clue.text: Accommodation provided for the rest of the players

definitions.text: Accommodation provided for the rest of the players

parts.words: Accommodation provided for the rest of the players
parts.note: rest seems to mean the other players, but it is their resting, in the room where actors wait when offstage

explanation.surface: A room set aside for the remaining members of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre lounge where performers relax before and between appearances on stage.

clue.text: Put in this month — date to be arranged

parts.note: inst., instant, is an old business abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: to be arranged suggests the four letters of date are reordered

explanation.surface: An appointment made this month, with the day still to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be arranged' reorders the second word into ATED; inst. is old commercial shorthand, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.'
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone in an office is to put them in post.

clue.text: Empowered to accept name-change, so acquiescent

indicators.note: to accept means the word for empowered takes in the reworked letters

parts.note: able means having the power or capacity

indicators.note: change here means the letters of name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone authorised to approve a rebrand, and happy to go along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' gives MENA, the anagram of the hyphenated word's first half; 'to accept' sets it inside after the first letter of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone compliant and willing goes along with what is asked.

clue.text: Hang-ups can give rise to irascibility in doctors

indicators.note: in places the word for bad temper inside the word for doctors

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors
bile is bad temper or irascibility

explanation.surface: Psychological hang-ups can make doctors grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang-ups' suggests complexes; it means things that hang, such as nursery decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging decorations of balanced pieces that turn in the air are things hung up.

clue.text: Little to impress English visitors in this city

indicators.note: little means only a small part of the words impress English is used

explanation.surface: A city not much interested in impressing English tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: The city lies across 'impress English'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr.

clue.text: Steps taken over a barrier without hesitation but to no avail

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the steps word surrounds the hesitation

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence or wall
er is a hesitation noise

explanation.surface: Climbing over a fence confidently but pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, a common old usage; a stile is a step or ladder over a British field fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fruitless or unproductive gives no result.

clue.text: Turn white at seeing a novice in shore

indicators.note: in places the novice letter inside the shore word

parts.note: a beach is a shore
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Someone goes pale at the sight of a beginner swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To blanch or whiten is to lose colour.

clue.text: Underhand writer makes a bloomer

parts.note: a lob is an underarm throw or bowl
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A sly author commits a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flowering plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Nothing upset the American legal official, a woman

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for nothing is turned upside down

parts.note: nil means nothing
a DA is a district attorney in the USA

explanation.surface: Nothing could ruffle the US prosecutor, a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a female first name.

clue.text: The touching line of a man on strike

indicators.note: on in an across clue sets the man word after the strike word

parts.note: to tan is to beat or strike
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A man who has walked out in an industrial dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on strike' looks like industrial action, but 'on' is the across convention for placing one piece after another, and strike means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a straight line that meets a curve at one point is touching it.

clue.text: A team batting is exhausted

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the side at the crease is the one in, the whole of them

explanation.surface: The batting side is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the team batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted people are worn out; and a whole team batting is everyone inside.

clue.text: He coined a new word for one breaking the record first

indicators.note: breaking says the three letters of one are broken up and reordered

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
1st, written with the numeral as I, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A record-breaker who invented a term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns ONE into NEO; 1ST is read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who invents fresh vocabulary.

clue.text: Saves men making personal commitment

definitions.meaning: conserves or economises, as with resources
married men, who have made a vow

explanation.surface: Economy, and men who make vows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saves' looks like a noun; it is the verb to economise.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to manage them thriftily; married men are spouses.

clue.text: Approach both single and married and hang the outcome!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
to pend is to hang, from Latin pendere

explanation.surface: Advice to court both singles and married people regardless of what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outcome!' is a flourish of the surface, as in 'hang the consequences'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something looming draws near.
